memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD answered Moses, 'Go out in front of the people. Take with you some of
the elders of Israel and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the
Nile, and go. I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the
rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink.' So Moses did this
in the sight of the elders of Israel." - Ex 17:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's answer is full of striking details.

First, the same staff that struck the Nile and turned it to blood will now bring
water from a rock. The instrument of judgment becomes the instrument of
provision.

Second, and this is remarkable: "I will stand there before you by the rock." God
positions Himself at the rock. When Moses strikes it, he is striking where God
has chosen to stand.

Third, the elders are witnesses. God does this in the open.

Paul, writing to the Corinthians about Israel in the wilderness, says something
that has caught Christian attention ever since: "they drank from the spiritual
rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ" (1 Cor 10:4). That is not
a stretched allegory invented by later readers. It is the apostle's own
inspired comment on this event.

So the picture stands. A rock struck, at the place where God stood, and life
pouring out for thirsty, complaining people who had just accused Him of wanting
them dead.

That is the shape of the gospel, and it was drawn in a desert long before
Calvary.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you come to Christ for water, or are you still striking other rocks?
2. What has God provided for you at cost to Himself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You are the rock from whom living water flows. Thank You that You
were struck so that I could drink. Amen.
